elements_not_encoded.text: First assess and manage airway, breathing, circulation and level of consciousness 16.
elements_not_encoded.reason: ABC assessment and management, pointer to page 16.

elements_not_encoded.text: Identify all injuries and look for cause, undress patient and assess front and back. If injured, use log-roll to turn. Then cover and keep warm.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Examination and handling steps (undress, log-roll, keep warm).

elements_not_encoded.text: If seizures 20, if injuries 30, if burns 31.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Pointers to pages 20 (seizures), 30 (injuries), 31 (burns); those pages hold the logic, and seizure/burns/injury are already warning signs.

elements_not_encoded.text: Check glucose, temperature and pupils:
elements_not_encoded.reason: Instruction heading the decision tree. Glucose and temperature are routine vitals (no measure task); pupil findings are cited at the leaves.

elements_not_encoded.text: Glucose
elements_not_encoded.reason: Tree node label 'Glucose' (routine vital); its threshold leaves are handled separately.

elements_not_encoded.text: Temperature
elements_not_encoded.reason: Tree node label 'Temperature' (routine vital); its threshold leaves are handled separately.

elements_not_encoded.text: Pupils
elements_not_encoded.reason: Tree node label 'Pupils'; pupil findings are cited at the leaves.

elements_not_encoded.text: < 3 (< 4 if diabetes) or unable to measure
elements_not_encoded.reason: Low-glucose branch leads only to dextrose/thiamine management and names no diagnosis, so no rule consumes it ('unable to measure' also has no representation).
Temperature ≤ 35°C branch leads only to warming management and names no diagnosis.

elements_not_encoded.text: Unequal or
elements_not_encoded.reason: Unequal pupils branch leads only to management (raise head, discuss) and names no diagnosis; not checked for because nothing would consume it.

elements_not_encoded.text: respond poorly to light
elements_not_encoded.reason: Poor pupil light response branch leads only to management and names no diagnosis.

elements_not_encoded.text: Give fluids:
Remove cold/ wet clothing and cover with warm blankets.
Raise head by 30 degrees.
Give dextrose 10%2 5mL/ kg IV. If known alcohol user, give thiamine 200mg IM before dextrose.
If injured, keep body straight and tilt to raise head (avoid bending spine).
Warm IV fluids to 40°C (avoid cold fluids).
If patient was in malaria area in past 3 months, manage 39.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Malaria travel pointer to page 39 ('manage'); not a 'consider' statement on this page.

elements_not_encoded.text: Also give sodium chloride 0.9% 15-20mL/kg 4 IV over the first hour, then 10mL/kg/ hour thereafter.
If no response or temperature ≤ 32°C, also use a warming device.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Warming device; the ≤ 32°C threshold only gates management.

elements_not_encoded.text: If temperature > 40°C:
Discuss urgently with referral centre.
Remove clothing.
Recheck glucose after 15 minutes: if still < 3, give further dextrose 10%2 2mL/kg IV.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Glucose recheck and repeat dextrose dose.

elements_not_encoded.text: Use fan and water spray to cool patient.
If known kidney/heart disease, discuss fluid volume with doctor.
Apply ice-packs to axillae, groin and neck.
Then give dextrose 5%3 or 10% 1L IV 6 hourly.
Stop if breathing worsens.
If known diabetes and referral delay > 2 hours, discuss with referral centre before giving short-acting insulin 0.1units/ kg IM5. Insulin may cause low potassiu
Refer urgently.
While awaiting transport:
elements_not_encoded.reason: Heading for monitoring while awaiting transport.

elements_not_encoded.text: Check BP, pulse, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation and GCS every 15 minutes. Insert urinary catheter.
If BP < 90/60, pulse > 100 or < 50, respiratory rate > 20 or < 9, oxygen saturation < 94% or drop in GCS, reassess and manage airway, breathing, circulation and
elements_not_encoded.reason: Reassessment trigger while awaiting transport, routing back to page 16; monitoring, not triage.

judgment_calls.decision: or of Decreased level of consciousness and the AVPU levels below Alert that triage records (reacts to voice, reacts to pain, unresponsive); 'Confused' (Clouded consciousness) left out because confusion is its own presentation.
judgment_calls.alternatives: Decreased level of consciousness alone (would rarely fire for adults, as it is not an adult common symptom or warning sign); include Clouded consciousness.

judgment_calls.topic: Shock line inside the glucose ≥ 11.1 branch
judgment_calls.decision: Probable shock = decreased consciousness AND glucose ≥ 11.1 AND any of SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100, RR > 30, weakness; the comma list read as 'any of'.
judgment_calls.alternatives: All four required; or not gated by glucose (the line sits only in the ≥ 11.1 column).

judgment_calls.decision: Probable Overdose and probable Poisoning both fire from dilated pupils of both eyes; the poisoning rule repeats the pupil evidence instead of using active_condition Overdose so its evidence is checked for in this file.
judgment_calls.alternatives: Poisoning only from the pinpoint branches (if the connector were read as not joining).

judgment_calls.decision: Low glucose, temperature ≤ 35°C and unequal/poorly reactive pupils lead only to management; not encoded and not checked for (Will: remove findings nothing consumes).
judgment_calls.alternatives: Invent hypoglycaemia / hypothermia / raised intracranial pressure diagnoses (rejected: not on the page).

judgment_calls.decision: Single Urgent rule for any decreased consciousness, matching 'Give urgent attention'; no escalation for probable poisoning although Poisoning is a Very urgent adult warning sign.
judgment_calls.alternatives: Very urgent when Poisoning is probable.
